title: The sun itself will be folded up.
subtitle: The first sign of the end
then: Ibn Kathir explains that takwir means folding one part of something into another, {idea}like folding a turban.{/idea} The sun will be rolled up and its light will go. The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever wants to see the Day of Judgement {reward}as if with his own eyes{/reward} should read this surah.
now: You plan your life around sunrise alarms and sunset dinners. {idea}The one thing you never doubt will be wrapped up like cloth.{/idea} Everything you lean on that is not Allah has an expiry.
old: Some things in life are simply permanent.
new: Even the sun will be folded away. Only Allah does not end.
try: Watch the sun rise or set today and remember it is on loan.

title: The stars will scatter and fall.
subtitle: The night sky poured out
then: Ibn Kathir says it means {trap}when they are scattered{/trap}, citing 82:2. The root of the word means to be poured out. Ubayy bin Kab described people {idea}in their marketplaces{/idea} when the sun's light goes and then the stars scatter.
now: You are in the supermarket queue, scrolling, planning the weekend. {idea}Ubayy pictured the end arriving on a normal market day.{/idea} Nothing about an ordinary day makes it safe from being the last one.
old: The end will come with lots of warning, on some dramatic day.
new: It may arrive on an ordinary day, while I am busy shopping.
try: Do one good deed today that you have been saving for a quieter time.

title: Mountains will move and be gone.
subtitle: The most solid thing turns to nothing
then: Ibn Kathir explains the mountains {trap}will not remain in their places and they will be destroyed.{/trap} Then {idea}the earth will be left as a flat, level plain.{/idea} The surah keeps listing what people thought could never move.
now: You call your job rock solid and your house your foundation. {idea}The verse moves actual rock.{/idea} It gently asks what you are standing on underneath all that.
old: My life is built on solid ground.
new: Only my bond with Allah is solid. Even mountains move.
try: Make a short dua today asking Allah to be your firm footing, by name.

title: The most precious camels, left untended.
subtitle: When the most valuable thing stops mattering
then: Ibn Kathir says the 'Ishar were {reward}the best type of camel{/reward}, especially those near giving birth. On that Day {trap}they will not be milked or tied up{/trap}, abandoned by owners for whom they used to be the most important thing.
now: Your new phone, your car with no scratches, your investment app you open ten times a day. {trap}One day you will walk past it without a glance.{/trap} Hold it now with that in mind.
old: My most valuable possession deserves my constant attention.
new: The things I guard most will be the first I forget on that Day.
try: Give away or lend one thing you are a little too attached to.

title: Wild beasts gathered, even the flies.
subtitle: No creature is forgotten
then: Ibn Kathir cites 6:38: every creature and bird are {idea}communities like you{/idea}, gathered to their Lord. Ibn Abbas said, {reward}everything will be gathered, even the flies.{/reward} Animals that fled people will crowd together with them.
now: You kick a stray cat away from the bins, or forget to feed the pet when you are busy. {idea}That animal is also part of the gathering.{/idea} How you treated it is not invisible.
old: How I treat animals does not really count.
new: Every creature is gathered by Allah, and my kindness to them is seen.
try: Do one kind thing for an animal today, even putting out water.

title: The seas set ablaze.
subtitle: Water becomes fire
then: Ibn Kathir links this to 52:6, the sea kindled. He cites Ali, who said of this verse {trap}the seas become as blazing fire.{/trap} In the account of Ubayy, {idea}the jinn rush to the sea and find it aflame.{/idea}
now: You stand on the beach at sunset feeling calm, the waves cool on your feet. {idea}Allah made it calm, and He can change it.{/idea} The calm you feel is a mercy, not a guarantee.
old: The natural world will always behave as it does today.
new: Every calm thing I enjoy is held in place by Allah's mercy.
try: Next time you drink water, pause and thank Allah that it is cool.

title: Every soul paired with its own kind.
subtitle: You will be grouped with those you resemble

row.title: its peers
sub: those who did the same deeds

then: Ibn Kathir explains {idea}every type of soul will be gathered with its peer.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said each man will be with {reward}the people who performed the same deeds that he did{/reward}, and cited the three groups in 56:7-10.
now: Look at the five people you message most. Look at what you do together. {idea}That is a preview of your group.{/idea} You can still choose who you become like.
old: My friends do not say much about where I am headed.
new: I will be gathered with those whose deeds match mine.
try: Reach out today to one friend who makes you better, and spend some time with them.

title: The buried girl will be asked.
subtitle: The voiceless one is given a voice

row.title: the wronged
sub: asked first, in front of him

then: In the time before Islam, some {trap}buried infant girls in the dirt out of hatred of girls.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains that on the Day, the girl herself will be asked. {idea}If the one wronged is questioned, what should the wrongdoer expect?{/idea}
now: Think of the person at work or at home you could brush aside because they would never complain. {idea}Allah gives the silent ones a voice on that Day.{/idea} How you treat the powerless is on record.
old: If the person I wronged never spoke up, it is over.
new: Allah will give a voice to everyone who could not speak for themselves.
try: Make it right with one person you know you treated unfairly and who never said anything.

title: For what sin was she killed?
subtitle: A question with no answer

row.title: a path back
sub: the Prophet ﷺ gave Qays one

then: Ibn Abbas and others said she will {idea}ask, demanding restitution for her blood.{/idea} Ibn Kathir also reports that Qays bin Asim came to the Prophet ﷺ confessing he had done this before Islam, and {reward}was given a way to atone.{/reward}
now: There is something in your past you would rather never be asked about. {reward}The door Qays walked through is still open to you.{/reward} The question is coming either way, so turn back while you can.
old: What I did before is too dark to ever be forgiven.
new: Allah's question is coming, and so is a door back if I turn now.
try: Make sincere tawbah today for one specific old wrong, and do one good deed to follow it.

title: The pages you dictated, opened.
subtitle: Your record handed to you
then: Ad-Dahhak said {idea}every person will be given his paper in his right hand or in his left.{/idea} Qatadah said: O son of Adam, it is written, rolled up, then given to you. {reward}So let each look at what he himself dictated.{/reward}
now: Your phone keeps a screen-time report every week, and you avoid opening it. {idea}There is another report you are writing right now, line by line.{/idea} You are the one dictating it.
old: Most of my day is too small to be recorded.
new: I am dictating my own record, and I can choose what goes in today.
try: Before bed, look back on today and add one good line on purpose: a dua, a kindness, an apology.

title: The sky peeled back.
subtitle: Nothing left covered
then: Mujahid said {idea}it is drawn away.{/idea} As-Suddi said {trap}stripped off.{/trap} After the pages are opened, the sky itself is pulled back. {reward}The whole scene is about things being uncovered.{/reward}
now: You close the door, turn the screen away, and feel unseen. {idea}Nothing is above your head that blocks Allah's sight.{/idea} That can feel heavy, or it can feel like company.
old: There are moments when no one at all is watching.
new: Nothing is ever really hidden from Allah, in this life or the next.
try: In one private moment today, do the thing you would do if you remembered Allah sees you.

title: The Fire is stoked.
subtitle: A warning given while there is time
then: As-Suddi said {trap}it is heated.{/trap} The surah has moved from the sky to the Fire. {idea}It is described to people still alive in Makkah, who could still choose.{/idea}
now: Your car dashboard shows a warning light. You can ignore it or pull over. {idea}A warning given early is a mercy.{/idea} The verse is that light on your dashboard.
old: Talk of the Fire is meant to scare me into giving up.
new: Allah warns me early because He wants me to turn back.
try: Ask Allah tonight, in your own words, to protect you and your family from the Fire.

title: And Paradise is brought close.
subtitle: The reward brought to its people
then: Ad-Dahhak, Abu Malik, Qatadah and others said {reward}it will be brought near to its inhabitants.{/reward} Right after the Fire is stoked, {idea}Paradise is set close.{/idea} Both are real, both are ready.
now: You picture Paradise as something for the very pious, far beyond you. {reward}The verse has it moving toward its people.{/reward} Each small good thing today is a step toward meeting it.
old: Paradise feels distant and meant for better people than me.
new: Paradise will be brought near to those who reached for it.
try: Ask Allah for Paradise by name today, as specifically as you can.

title: Then each soul knows what it brought.
subtitle: The answer to every when
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {idea}the conclusive response of the previous statements.{/idea} When all of it happens, every soul will know what it has done. He cites 3:30: {reward}every person will find all the good he did, present.{/reward}
now: You pack for a trip and only at the airport realise what you forgot. {idea}On that Day you will see exactly what you packed.{/idea} The packing is happening now, in your ordinary days.
old: I will sort out my deeds properly at some later point.
new: I am packing what I will bring right now, every day.
try: Add one deed to your bag today that you would be glad to find on that Day.
